paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God means what He says, and He tells the truth even when it's hard to hear. He told Aaron plainly that he would not enter the land, "because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah" (Numbers 20:24). I think that one hurts, and I'm not going to rush past it.

Now look at what else is in this passage. God didn't leave Aaron guessing, and He didn't leave His people without a priest. Aaron's garments went on his son Eleazar, and the work kept going (Numbers 20:26, 28). One servant's time ended, and God's plan kept right on moving.

And Israel didn't act like it was nothing. The whole house of Israel "mourned for him thirty days" (Numbers 20:29). Honest grief is not a lack of faith, baker. So take God at His word, take His commands seriously, and when loss comes, let yourself mourn and trust Him with what comes next.
